main.title: What If You Woke Up 300 Million Years Ago?
main.description:
You open your eyes and a dragonfly with 70 cm wings is sitting on your chest.
The air is almost one-third oxygen, and one spark can set the whole forest on fire.

Real science in this video:
- 300 million years ago, oxygen was around 30% of the air (today it's 21%).
- Giant clubmoss trees stood about 30 m tall, and there were no flowers, grass or birds yet.
- Griffinflies like Meganeura had wings about 70 cm across; Arthropleura, a millipede-like giant, was about 2.6 m long.
- The land that became India sat far to the south under ice; glacial boulder beds in Odisha (Talchir) still show it.
- Buried swamp forests became coal, and coal makes about three-quarters of India's electricity today.

Chapters:
0:00 You wake up
0:32 Minute 1 · The air
1:02 Hour 1 · The forest
1:35 Hour 3 · The giants
2:27 Night 1 · The fire
3:05 Year 1 · Where is India?
3:35 Today · The twist

Nobody can travel back in time. This is a thought experiment built on real research, and some numbers (like the exact oxygen level) are still debated by scientists.

If you could bring one thing back from that world, what would you pick?

Sources:
Krause et al. 2018, Nature Communications (oxygen history): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6172248
Natural History Museum, giant dragonflies: https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/giant-dragonflies.html
University of Cambridge, Arthropleura (Davies et al. 2021): https://www.cam.ac.uk/stories/giantmillipede
Glasspool & Scott 2010, fossil charcoal and oxygen (Field Museum): https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2010-08/fm-oft080210.php
Geological Survey of India, Gondwana coal: https://fossil.energy.gov/international/Publications/ucg_1106_gsi.pdf
Ember, India electricity data: https://ember-energy.org/countries-and-regions/india
